Choose gear that earns its place

Build a pack around the work and conditions.

Equipment · 4 min read · Updated 2026-11-24

Fit before features

Start with a pack that can hold your chosen load securely and fits comfortably. Check seams, straps and buckles. Use footwear that suits the surface and has been worn in training.

Pack for the route

Bring water, weather-appropriate clothing, a light when needed and a way to navigate and contact help. Longer or remote outings may require additional equipment; plan around the actual conditions rather than a fixed list.

Test the setup

Try changes on a short familiar route. Note pressure points, loose items and what you actually use. A simple dependable setup is often more useful than a complicated one you have not tested.

Test equipment before buying more

Make a short checklist for pack security, footwear, clothing, visibility and water. Try the current setup on a familiar route, note a specific limitation, then change one item. A heavier or more expensive product is not automatically better. Keep essential safety equipment appropriate to the route, and do not test unfamiliar equipment for the first time at a demanding event.
